note: Fragments read: his firm raised buildings 'on average six feet without causing them any damage' (the Matteson House, 1859; the Tremont House, 1861); his first sleeping car 'was finished in 1864'; Lincoln's body went home to Springfield in a sleeper and 'hundreds of thousands of people lined the route in homage'; in 1894 he cut wages but 'he didn't reduce the rent in Pullman'; he 'died of a heart attack' on 19 October 1897; his family had him buried in a 'lead-lined mahogany coffin, which was then sealed inside a block of concrete', under steel rails 'bolted together at right angles', at Graceland Cemetery.
